So, we last talked in June. You were about to head into renewal season and you told me, very kindly, that you didn't have room for a new tool until it was over. Fair.

[Hold up a sticky note that says "Q3 renewals: done?"]

By my count, that season should be wrapped up now. And I'm curious how it went. Specifically: how many of the accounts that churned were ones your team saw coming?

[Beat]

Because when we talked, you said something that stuck with me: that your CSMs usually knew an account was in trouble about two weeks after it was too late to do anything about it. That's the gap Beacon is built for. We pull product usage, support tickets, and survey data into a single health score so the warning shows up while there's still time to act.

[Turn laptop toward camera showing a simple health dashboard with fictional accounts]

This is what it looked like for a company about your size. The red ones are the accounts that would have been surprises.

I'm not asking for a full evaluation. I'd love 20 minutes to hear how renewals went and show you what Beacon would have flagged in hindsight if you'd been running it since June. If the answer is "we caught everything," then honestly, congratulations, and I'll go find someone who needs me more.

[Smile, raise mug]

Link to my calendar is below. Thanks, Freya.
quality_notes: Playful without being gimmicky, recalls the exact reason for the pause and a memorable buyer quote, and proposes a low-commitment hindsight analysis.

subject: Introduction via Josephine Arkwright
message:
Dear Mr. Ostrander,

Josephine Arkwright suggested I write to you. She and I worked together when her legal team at Coralline Bio adopted Draftkit last year, and she mentioned that Helixway is now negotiating a high volume of clinical trial agreements with research sites.

At Coralline, Josephine's team reduced first-turn time on site agreements from about six business days to two, primarily by standardizing fallback clauses and letting the contracts team handle routine redlines without escalating to counsel.

I would welcome the opportunity to understand how your team currently manages CTA negotiations and whether a similar approach might be useful. Would a 30-minute conversation in the next two weeks be convenient? I am glad to work around your schedule.

Kind regards,
Eleanor Fairweather
buyer_reply: Ms. Fairweather, thank you. Josephine mentioned you might be in touch. We have roughly 60 site agreements in flight and the backlog is a real concern. My assistant will reach out to schedule.
quality_notes: Formal tone fits the persona, names the referrer and a specific peer outcome relevant to the buyer's current workload, and makes a clear, modest request.

message: Hi Nadia, Tobias at Ledgerline. Congrats on the 4-day close last month! Know any other CFOs fighting month-end? Happy to send you a referral credit if an intro turns into anything.
buyer_reply: Ha thanks. Let me think on it.
quality_notes: Friendly and specific about the result, but leads with an incentive in a way that can feel transactional and gives no guidance on who to refer.

subject: Picking up from Kofi's evaluation
message:
Hi Desmond,

I worked with Kofi Mensah last year when he was evaluating Patchbay to replace Bellweather's homegrown integration layer. When Kofi left in August, the project went quiet, which is completely understandable.

I'm reaching out because I know the evaluation surfaced a few things that might still be useful to you regardless of what you decide: an inventory of 37 active integrations, which ones were failing most often, and a rough estimate of engineering hours spent on maintenance. Kofi had planned to bring it to you.

Would it help if I sent that summary over? If after reading it you think the problem is worth solving, we can talk. If not, at least you'll have the inventory.

Rhiannon
buyer_reply: Thanks, but we've decided to rebuild that layer internally with our platform team. I'd still take the summary if you're offering.
quality_notes: Smart to offer the prior evaluation's artifacts as standalone value, but doesn't anticipate the build-vs-buy objection a new CTO is likely to have, leaving little to work with in the reply.

subject: 12 new studios, same scheduling spreadsheet?
message:
Lorcan,

Read that Pulsehouse is opening 12 studios across Texas and Arizona next year. Congratulations.

When we spoke 10 months ago you had 18 locations and your managers were building instructor schedules in a shared spreadsheet. You said it was "annoying, but survivable." At 30 locations, with instructors covering multiple studios, survivable usually stops being true. Double-bookings and last-minute coverage gaps start showing up in member reviews.

Shiftwell handles multi-location instructor scheduling, swaps, and certification tracking. Two other boutique fitness chains about your size rolled it out before expansion rather than during, and both said that was the right order.

Worth 25 minutes before your Q1 openings?

Akosua
quality_notes: Concise, uses the trigger event and the buyer's own earlier words to show why the problem changes at scale, and suggests a timing-specific next step.

message: Hi Ingrid!! Following up AGAIN on Vaultline. Your competitors are all getting SOC 2 certified and you're going to fall behind if you don't act now. I've sent 6 emails, can you just give me 15 min? This week only I can get you priority onboarding.
quality_notes: Pushy and guilt-trippy, references the number of unanswered emails, invents competitive pressure, and dangles a meaningless 'priority onboarding' offer.

subject: A request regarding your portfolio peers
message:
Dear Wendell,

Thank you again for the time during last week's quarterly review. The reduction in your monthly cloud spend, from roughly $410K to $318K since April, has been a highlight for our team as well.

You mentioned that Riverlight's investors hold a few other media and gaming companies that are scaling their infrastructure quickly. If any of their technology leaders would benefit from a conversation, I would be grateful for an introduction. I am happy to draft a short note that you could forward, so it requires as little of your time as possible.

With appreciation,
Samira Haddad
buyer_reply: Happy to. Send me the draft and I'll forward it to the CTO at Glimmerbox; they're getting crushed on GPU spend.
quality_notes: Uses concrete results and offers to draft the forward, which is helpful, but the ask is somewhat vague and could suggest a specific peer or profile.

message:
Hi Jun, Felix Morrow from Onramp. Got two minutes?

[If yes]
Thanks. You started a trial with us in August, set up the Google Workspace and laptop provisioning connectors, and then it went quiet after the first week. I'm not calling to chase you. I'm calling because usually when a trial stalls at that point it's for one of three reasons: the connector setup was more work than expected, a bigger priority showed up, or the tool just didn't fit. Which was it for you?

[Listen]

[If setup friction]
That's on us. Our solutions engineer, Aria, can do the remaining setup with you in one 45-minute session. You'd see a full new-hire flow running end to end. Want me to book it?

[If priority shift]
Understood. When does your next hiring wave start? I'd rather reconnect two weeks before that than bug you now.

[If bad fit]
I appreciate the honesty. Can you tell me what was missing? It genuinely helps us, and I'll close out the trial so it's not sitting there.

[Close]
Thanks Jun. I'll send a short recap email either way.
quality_notes: Clear, respectful structure with branches for common stall reasons, but stays generic and doesn't use anything from the trial data to show Felix understands Stonefield's onboarding pain.

subject: Forecast calls at Gridwell
message:
Hi Marcus,

Saw you landed at Gridwell as VP Sales. Congratulations, that's a big jump and a great team.

At Tessaro you were the person who got our forecasting rollout across the line, and I still quote your line about "forecast calls being a weekly hostage negotiation." I'm guessing the first thing you're doing in the new seat is figuring out how much you can trust the pipeline you inherited.

When you get to that point, I'd be glad to do what we did at Tessaro in the first month: connect Pipewise to the CRM read-only and give you a snapshot of stage aging, slip rates, and coverage by rep. No contract, just a baseline you can take into your first board meeting.

No rush. Settle in first.

Nora
buyer_reply: Nora! Ha, I still say that line. Honestly the inherited pipeline is about what you'd expect. Let's do the read-only snapshot. I'll get you a contact in RevOps by Friday.
quality_notes: Re-engages a former champion at a new company by recalling shared success, anticipates his first-90-days need, and offers a no-commitment baseline he can use personally.

message: Hello Anselm, Lucinda Achterberg at Halyard Ventures suggested I reach out. She mentioned you have taken over board preparation at Codewright ahead of your first independent director joining. Several of Halyard's portfolio companies use Quorum HQ to run board packs and investor updates. Would a brief call be useful as you set up the process?
quality_notes: Investor-sourced intro with a precise trigger (first independent director) and a modest, relevant ask; appropriately formal for a chief of staff.

message:
[Opening]
Hi Dr. Park, this is Benedikt Sallow from Tallyhouse. Do you have a few minutes, or should I call back at a better time?

[If yes]
Thank you. I'll keep it brief. Westbrook looked at Tallyhouse about a year and a half ago, before you joined, when the procurement office was trying to get a handle on departmental purchasing. The project paused during the budget freeze. I saw you came in as CFO this summer, and given your background at the state university system, I suspect vendor spend is somewhere on your list.

[Discovery]
Can I ask how you're thinking about it?

Specifically, do you have a clear view today of what each department is spending with outside vendors, and how much of that goes through a contract versus a purchasing card?

[Listen]

One thing that came up in the original evaluation was that about 30 percent of departmental spend was going through p-cards with no PO, mostly software subscriptions and event services. The procurement team estimated a fair amount of duplication, like three departments paying separately for the same survey tool.

Does that match what you're seeing?

[Listen. If yes, continue. If no, ask what's changed.]

[Bridge]
What we typically do with a new CFO is run a spend analysis on the last 12 months of AP and card data. It takes about two weeks, it doesn't require you to buy anything, and it usually surfaces a handful of consolidation opportunities you can act on right away. Several schools have used it to build their case for the next budget cycle.

[Ask]
Would it make sense to set up 30 minutes with you and whoever owns procurement now to scope that?

[If hesitant]
Completely understand. Would it be useful if I sent a one-page summary of what the original evaluation found, so you have it as background?

[Close]
Thank you, Dr. Park. I'll follow up by email today.
quality_notes: Bridges a stalled deal to a new executive with relevant prior findings, asks good discovery questions, and offers a low-risk spend analysis tied to her budget cycle.

subject: Hey! Big ask :)
message:
Hey Gabriela!

Hope you're doing amazing! I wanted to reach out because I'm working on hitting my referral goal for Q4 and I thought of you since you've been such an awesome customer. As you know, Beacon CX has tons of great features like health scoring, playbooks, renewal forecasting, NPS integration, Slack alerts, executive dashboards, and our brand new AI churn predictor which is really cool.

I was wondering if you could think of anyone, honestly anyone, who might be interested? Could be people at your old companies, people in your CS community, LinkedIn connections, friends, whoever! The more the merrier. We also have a referral program where you can get a gift card if someone signs.

Also, while I have you, would you be open to doing a case study? And maybe a G2-style review? Our marketing team would love it.

Let me know! Thanks so much!!

Toby
buyer_reply: Hi Toby, I'll keep an eye out. Not really able to do a case study this quarter.
quality_notes: Makes the referral about the rep's quota, recites features the customer already owns, asks for 'anyone,' and piles on unrelated asks, which dilutes everything.

message: Isidore, Wren from Draftkit. Your trial expired with 3 NDAs uploaded but none redlined. Want a 15-min walkthrough of auto-redline on one of them before I archive it?
quality_notes: Specific about trial activity and offers a concrete next step, though it's a bit abrupt and the archive mention reads slightly like a threat.

subject: Intro from Selin at Mosaic Care
message:
Hi Ravi,

Selin Okonkwo from Mosaic Care gave me your name. She said you two met at the research ops conference in Denver and that you were trying to get your clinicians' interview notes and your patient interviews into one place.

At Mosaic, Selin's team uses Fieldnote to tag and search across roughly 300 interviews, and they've cut down the "has anyone ever asked patients about this?" questions in Slack considerably. She thought the setup they use for HIPAA-sensitive transcripts might be relevant to you.

Would you be up for a 20-minute call to compare notes? Happy to have Selin join if that's easier.

Ottilie
buyer_reply: Thanks Ottilie. Selin's been raving about it. The honest blocker is budget; research tooling got cut for H1. Could we talk in the spring?
quality_notes: Solid warm intro with a relevant peer outcome, but doesn't qualify budget or timing at all, so the conversation stalls on the first objection.

subject: No sales pitch, just checking in
message:
Hi Sunniva,

When you chose another vendor for your SOC 2 program in May, you were gracious about it and clear about why: their auditor partnership looked like it would get you to a report faster. That was a reasonable call.

I'm not writing to relitigate it. I'm writing because the auditor window most teams target for a first Type II is coming up in January, and that's usually when the gaps in an implementation show up, especially around evidence collection for vendor reviews and access reviews.

If things are on track, wonderful, and you can ignore this. If any part of it is stuck, I'm happy to spend 30 minutes giving you an outside read on where things stand, even if you stay with your current platform. We'd rather be useful than right.

Leopold
buyer_reply: Leopold, I appreciate this more than you know. The evidence collection is a mess and our auditor already flagged it. Let's talk. I'm not promising we'll switch.
quality_notes: Respectful closed-lost revival that acknowledges the buyer's decision, times outreach to a predictable pain point, and offers help without demanding a switch.

message: Hi Dominic, Harriet Quayle at Ledgerline. Saw the news that Orthavance acquired Kestrel Surgical. Congratulations. When we spoke last year you were closing in seven days with one entity. Integrating a second set of books usually adds a few days until the consolidation is automated. If that's on your radar, I'd like to show you how we handled it for another device company. My number is 312-555-0148. I'll send an email too.
quality_notes: Good trigger and a relevant problem statement, but the 'another device company' proof is vague and the voicemail could give a clearer reason to call back now.

message:
[Mateo on camera, casual setting]

Hey Bronwyn, it's Mateo from Shiftwell. Quick video because I think it's easier than another email.

First, thank you. Your managers at Saltgrass have been on Shiftwell for about eight months now, and the shift-swap approvals have gone from something your GMs complained about every week to something they mostly don't think about. That's a win and it's really your team's.

[Pause]

Here's why I'm recording this. When we talked last month you mentioned that your ownership group also runs the Tidewater Taproom locations, and that their scheduling is still done on paper at a few stores. I don't know the people over there, and I'd rather not cold call them out of nowhere.

Would you be open to introducing me to whoever runs ops or HR at Tidewater? Even a short email saying "this is the person who helped us with scheduling" would be plenty. If it's awkward because of internal politics, totally fine, just say so and I'll drop it.

Thanks, Bronwyn. Talk soon.
quality_notes: Specific and appreciative with a clearly scoped intro ask to a sister brand, but runs a bit long for what it's asking and doesn't offer to make the intro easy, such as drafting the email.

message: Hey Eamon, welcome to Thimble & Thread! I see you're the new VP Eng. Your company's AWS bill is probably out of control like everyone else's lol. Clearstack can cut it by 40% guaranteed. Want a demo?
buyer_reply: We're on GCP, and you don't know what our bill is. Pass.
quality_notes: Makes a wrong assumption about the cloud provider, guesses at the bill, and promises a 'guaranteed' 40% saving with no basis, which kills credibility instantly.

message: Stellan, thanks for the intro to Hollis at Caldera Metals yesterday. We're meeting Thursday. Really appreciate you vouching for us. Coffee's on me next time I'm in Dayton.
quality_notes: A short, specific thank-you that closes the loop on a referral, which reinforces the relationship and makes future referrals more likely.

subject: Onboarding 90 people in Q1
message:
Hi Thaddeus,

Congratulations on the Series C. The announcement mentioned growing from 210 to roughly 300 people by mid-year, mostly in lab operations.

When we talked in February, you decided the manual onboarding process was fine at your hiring pace then, about four people a month. At around 15 a month, the math changes. The people team becomes a bottleneck for accounts, lab safety training, equipment, and badge access, and new scientists lose their first week waiting on things.

Onramp automates the provisioning and checklist side, including role-specific steps like lab safety certification before badge activation. One of our genomics customers cut time-to-productive for new lab staff from eight days to three.

Would it be worth 30 minutes to map your Q1 hiring plan against what would need to happen for each new hire? Even if you don't buy anything, you'll leave with a clearer checklist.

Priscilla
quality_notes: Translates the funding announcement into a concrete operational consequence, recalls why the buyer said no before, and offers a planning session with standalone value.

message:
[Opening]
Hi Lavinia, this is Kwabena Hollis from Pipewise. Desmond Rourke at Tollgate suggested I give you a call; I believe he sent you a note on Monday. Is now an okay time?

[If yes]
Great, thanks. Desmond mentioned you two used to work together and that you've recently been asked to own the forecast at Freightmark. He thought it might be worth comparing notes, since his team went through something similar last year.

[Context]
For what it's worth, the short version of Desmond's story: their forecast was rolled up from rep commits in a spreadsheet, it was off by 20 to 30 percent most quarters, and the CRO was losing trust in it with the board. They used Pipewise to build a model based on deal history and activity, and within two quarters they were landing within about 6 percent.

But I don't want to assume your situation is the same. Can I ask a few questions?

[Discovery]
How is the forecast built today, and who owns each piece of it?

[Listen]

When the forecast misses, what usually turns out to be the cause? Deals slipping, deals that were never real, or upside that nobody saw?

[Listen]

And what's driving the change now? Is this coming from the CRO, the board, or your own push?

[Listen]

[Bridge]
That's helpful. Based on what you've described, the part that resonates most from Desmond's experience is probably the slip-rate analysis. It sounds like you know deals are slipping but not which ones or why.

[Ask]
What I'd suggest is a 45-minute session where we connect to a copy of your CRM data and show you historical slip patterns. If it's useful, we can talk about what a pilot looks like. If not, you'll still have the analysis.

Would next week work? I could also bring Desmond in for 10 minutes if you'd like to hear it from him directly.

[Close]
Thanks, Lavinia. I'll send a calendar invite and copy Desmond on the follow-up.
quality_notes: Uses the referrer's story as context rather than a pitch, asks focused discovery questions, and ties the next step to what the buyer actually said.

subject: How's the slide deck holding up?
message:
Hi Rory,

Last spring you told me Halcyon's board deck was "47 slides, 3 versions, and a prayer," and that you'd rather keep wrangling it than learn a new tool mid-fundraise. Totally fair.

Now that the round's closed and you've got two new board members, I'm guessing the deck has not gotten shorter. If the prayer part is still load-bearing, I'd be happy to show you how other hardware companies have moved their board packs into Quorum HQ.

Either way, good luck with the Q4 meeting.

Ines
buyer_reply: Ha. 52 slides now. Still praying. Maybe after the December meeting, I'm buried until then.
quality_notes: Uses the buyer's memorable phrase to good effect and keeps it light, but the ask is generic and doesn't propose a specific, easy next step tied to the December meeting.

message: Hi Constance, your CFO Hamish Leary asked me to connect with you directly. He's interested in getting renewal dates and contract owners for your top 50 vendors into one place before budget season. Could we find 30 minutes next week to see whether Tallyhouse fits how your team works today?
quality_notes: Clear top-down referral with a specific goal, but leaning on the CFO's name can feel like pressure on a direct report, and it doesn't ask about her own priorities.

message: Hi Celeste, it's Ulrich from Beacon CX, um, I hope you're doing well, I know it's been a while, I think we last talked maybe in the spring or early summer, and I know things were busy then and you mentioned you had a lot going on with the reorg and I totally understand that, those are always hard, anyway I just wanted to check in and see how things are going and whether you might have some time to reconnect at some point about Beacon, we've added a lot of new things, so, yeah, give me a call whenever, my number is, uh, 646-555-0193, thanks so much, bye.
quality_notes: Rambling, filler-heavy voicemail with no clear reason to call back, vague timing, and no specific value; the empathy comes across as unfocused rather than genuine.

subject: Draftkit: Comprehensive Contract Lifecycle Capabilities for Meridian Wave
message:
Dear Ms. Fairbanks,

I hope this message finds you well. My name is Augustin Pelletier and I am an Account Executive at Draftkit. I understand that you recently joined Meridian Wave Communications as Director of Legal Operations, and I would like to take this opportunity to congratulate you on your new role.

Meridian Wave evaluated Draftkit in the previous fiscal year. While the evaluation did not proceed at that time, I believe that our platform has evolved significantly and would now be an excellent fit. Draftkit offers clause library management, AI-assisted redlining, playbook enforcement, version comparison, approval workflows, e-signature integration, obligation tracking, reporting dashboards, a Microsoft Word add-in, SSO, role-based access control, and data residency options in multiple regions.

Additionally, our customers report significant efficiency gains, improved compliance, and reduced risk. We are trusted by leading organizations across many industries.

I would welcome the opportunity to schedule a 60-minute demonstration with you and your team at your earliest convenience. Please let me know your availability over the coming weeks.

Respectfully,
Augustin Pelletier
buyer_reply: Thank you. I'm still in my first month and not evaluating tools yet. Also, I'd want to understand why the previous evaluation stopped before revisiting.
quality_notes: Formal but bloated: a feature list, vague claims, and a 60-minute demo request to a new hire, with no curiosity about why the prior deal stalled, which the buyer has to point out.

message: Hi Kenji, Saoirse from Fieldnote. Your trial has 11 interviews tagged "pricing complaints" sitting there like an unread group chat. Want me to reopen it for a week so you can see the pattern?
buyer_reply: lol fair. yes, reopen it, we're redoing pricing in Jan anyway
quality_notes: Playful, short, and grounded in specific trial data that maps to a likely current priority; makes saying yes effortless.

message:
[Opening]
Hi Viktor, Esme Callaghan from Clearstack. We spoke back in April. Do you have three minutes?

[If yes]
Thanks. When we last talked, you decided to handle cost optimization in-house using your cloud provider's native tooling plus some scripts your team wrote. That was a sensible call. You had the people and the instinct to own it.

I'm calling for a specific reason. You launched Emberfall in October, and from what I read, player counts came in well above forecast. Congratulations. Launches like that usually do two things to a cloud bill: autoscaling groups that scale up and never quite come back down, and a pile of short-lived environments for hotfixes that nobody tears down.

[Question]
So I'm curious: how has the in-house approach held up through the launch?

[Listen]

[If "fine, we've got it handled"]
That's great to hear, and honestly not common. Out of curiosity, how much of your team's time is going into it each week? That's usually the hidden cost.

[Listen. If it's significant, continue to bridge. If not, close politely.]

[If "it's been rough" or "we haven't looked"]
That's what we hear from most studios post-launch. The native tools show you the spend, but they don't tell you who owns it or what's safe to turn off, and during a launch nobody has time to chase that down.

[Bridge]
Here's what I'd offer. We can connect to your billing data read-only, and within a day show you idle and orphaned resources by team, plus your commit coverage now that your usage baseline has shifted. It doesn't replace what your team built. A lot of customers keep their scripts and use us for visibility and accountability.

[Ask]
Would you be open to 30 minutes next week to look at that together?

[Close]
Thanks, Viktor. I'll send a short note with a couple of times. And congrats again on the launch.
quality_notes: Respects the buyer's build decision, ties the call to a concrete trigger with predictable cost side effects, and positions the product as complementary rather than a replacement.

subject: Your ISO 27001 timeline, and a small ask
message:
Hi Yetunde,

Congratulations on the ISO 27001 certification. Going from kickoff to certificate in five months, with SOC 2 already maintained in parallel, is fast, and your auditor's note about the quality of your evidence was well earned.

I have a small ask. In our last call you mentioned that you sit on the security working group for the HR tech founders' collective. If anyone in that group is about to start their first certification and is feeling overwhelmed, would you be comfortable pointing them my way? I'd be glad to just share the control mapping approach your team used, whether or not they become customers.

If that's not something you're comfortable with, no problem at all. Your success is the main thing.

Cormac
buyer_reply: Happy to. Two companies in the group are starting SOC 2 in Q1. I'll mention you at our next session on the 4th, and you can share the mapping doc with them.
quality_notes: Celebrates a specific customer achievement, targets a precise referral channel the customer mentioned, and offers value to prospects regardless of outcome.

message: Hey Mirela! Just checking in on Shiftwell. Any thoughts? Let me know!
quality_notes: Content-free check-in with no context about the trial, no value, and nothing for the buyer to respond to.

message: Lachlan, Fiona Keogh (we worked together at her old firm) said you're the person at Granitebay buried in lease amendments. She thought our lease-specific clause library might save your team some late nights. Happy to send a 3-minute video instead of a call if that's easier.
quality_notes: Casual warm intro with a credible connector, a pain point specific to the buyer's role, and a low-effort alternative to a meeting.

subject: Gross retention on the Q3 call
message:
Penelope,

On Innkeep's Q3 investor call, your CFO said gross retention dipped to 86 percent, mostly from mid-market churn, and that the company is adding eight CSMs to address it.

When we spoke in January, your team was at 91 percent and felt good about where things were, so I understand why Beacon wasn't a priority. Hiring CSMs will help with capacity. It won't tell them which accounts to call first.

If it's useful, I can show you how health scoring would have ranked your mid-market accounts this past summer.

Halvard
quality_notes: Uses a strong public trigger and makes a sharp point about capacity versus prioritization, but referencing the dip so bluntly may sting, and the ask lacks a concrete time or format.

message:
Hi Emil, I'm Rosalind with Ledgerline.

You and I haven't met. I worked with Delia Ortiz before she left Wayfarer in the summer. She and I spent a few months looking at how your team closes the books, and we'd gotten as far as mapping the reconciliations that were taking the longest, mostly the payment processor settlements and the deferred revenue rollforward.

When Delia moved on, the project naturally stopped, and I know you've had a lot to absorb as the new controller.

I'm recording this because I didn't want that work to disappear. If it's helpful, I'm happy to send you the reconciliation map Delia's team put together. It shows which accounts took the most time each month and why.

And if at some point you want to talk about automating any of it, I'd be glad to. No pressure either way. Thanks, Emil.
quality_notes: Considerate handoff to a replacement and offers useful prior work, but it's a little flat; it doesn't ask anything about Emil's own priorities or give a reason to act now.

message: Caspian, congrats on the CTO role. Briefcase's integration backlog came up a lot in our talks with your predecessor: 9 customer-requested connectors, 2 engineers. If you're rethinking build vs. buy for that, I can share how two similar-size legal tech teams handled it. Interested?
buyer_reply: Possibly. I want to get my bearings first. Ping me in about six weeks.
quality_notes: Tight, specific DM that uses known context about the backlog and frames the conversation as a strategic choice for the new CTO rather than a product pitch.

message: Ashton, busy season onboarding went great, 41 new associates and zero laptop delays! If you know another firm IT lead who'd want the playbook, I'd love an intro.
buyer_reply: Yep, will send you to Noor at Castlerigg CPA. She was asking me about it.
quality_notes: Upbeat and specific about results, but the ask is generic and could be more targeted or offer to make the intro easier.

subject: After the reorg
message:
Hi Siobhan,

I heard about the sales reorg at Ridgeway in September, and that you're now running both the broker and direct teams. That's a lot of change in a short time, and I imagine you're still sorting out who's covering what.

When we talked earlier in the year, the forecasting project paused because leadership was in flux. I don't want to push something on you before you're ready. But if part of the challenge right now is getting a reliable read on two teams' pipelines that were built differently, that's something Pipewise is good at.

Whenever it makes sense, I'm happy to talk.

Siobhan, take care of yourself in the meantime.

Bartholomew
quality_notes: Empathetic and aware of the reorg, but the value statement is generic and the open-ended close makes it easy to set aside indefinitely.

message: Good afternoon, Mr. Osei. This is Cressida Malone with Quorum HQ. I read that Sunmere has added two independent directors, including a former utility commissioner. Congratulations. When we last spoke, your board materials were coordinated over email with your general counsel, which worked well for a five-person board. With seven members and a new audit committee, many CEOs find a single secure portal reduces version confusion and last-minute requests. I would be glad to share how one renewables company set up committee workspaces. You can reach me at 617-555-0126. Thank you.
quality_notes: Polished voicemail that names a precise trigger, recalls the previous setup, explains why it breaks at the new board size, and offers a specific peer example.

subject: Introduction to the small business team?
message:
Hi Desmond,

Your research team's Fieldnote repository crossed 1,000 tagged sessions this month. More useful than the number: your quarterly insights review cited 23 interviews from the repository, and the consumer lending team used three of them to kill a feature before it was built.

You mentioned that the small business banking group runs its own research with a contractor and doesn't have access to any of this. I think there's a real opportunity there: they could search your consumer interviews for overlapping themes, and vice versa.

Would you be open to introducing me to whoever leads research or product for small business? I'd propose a short session where you show them what your team has built, and I'll stay in the background unless questions come up about setup or licensing.

Anouk
quality_notes: Internal expansion referral grounded in specific outcomes, frames the intro as mutually beneficial, and lets the champion lead the conversation.

subject: Sorry to hear about the layoffs - perfect time for Tallyhouse!
message:
Hi Lucia,

I was so sorry to see the news about the layoffs at Inkwell. That must be really tough for everyone.

The good news is that this is the perfect time to look at Tallyhouse again! With a smaller team, you'll need to do more with less, and our platform automates procurement so you won't miss the people you let go. We also typically find 10-15% savings in vendor spend, which could help avoid future cuts.

Let me know when you have time for a demo!

Garrett
buyer_reply: This is in very poor taste. Please don't contact me again.
quality_notes: Tone-deaf: opens with sympathy and immediately calls layoffs 'the good news,' implies software replaces the people let go, and pushes a demo during a painful moment.

subject: Introduction via Corvid Cloud Services
message:
Dear Mr. Kiplagat,

Our partners at Corvid Cloud Services, who manage part of Tradewind's infrastructure, suggested I contact you. They mentioned that Tradewind is reviewing cloud costs ahead of its 2027 budget and that cost allocation by business unit has been difficult.

Clearstack provides cost allocation and optimization, and several of Corvid's clients use it alongside their managed services. I would be pleased to arrange a short conversation, with Corvid present if you prefer.

Kind regards,
Henrietta Vos
buyer_reply: Thank you. Please send some materials first and I'll review with my team.
quality_notes: Professional partner-sourced intro with a relevant pain point, but thin on specifics or proof, which leads to a 'send materials' deflection.

message:
[Opening]
Hi Dashiell, Marguerite Osei from Vaultline. You and I talked in the spring about SOC 2. Is now a bad time?

[If okay]
I'll be direct, since I think this is time-sensitive for you. When we spoke, you said SOC 2 was a "next year" item because no customer had required it yet. Your VP of Sales, Odette, reached out to us yesterday. She said a large retail prospect paused a six-figure deal because Streamcraft doesn't have a SOC 2 report, and their procurement team wants at least a Type I before signing.

I wanted to talk to you before anything else happens, because ultimately this is your call and your team's workload, not sales'.

[Question]
Has that deal made its way to you yet?

[Listen]

[Context]
Here's the realistic picture. With an automated platform and an auditor who can move quickly, a Type I in about eight to ten weeks is achievable for a company your size, assuming your controls are in decent shape. That's often enough to unblock a deal like this, with a Type II to follow.

What usually slows teams down isn't the audit. It's collecting evidence and writing policies. That's where Vaultline does most of the work.

[Ask]
Would you be open to a 30-minute readiness assessment this week? We'll look at your current controls, give you an honest estimate of the timeline, and you can decide whether it's realistic for this deal or not. Odette is welcome to join, or not, whatever you prefer.

[If he pushes back on timing]
Understood. Even if this deal isn't the right forcing function, it's likely not the last customer who will ask. The assessment will tell you how far you are either way.

[Close]
Thanks, Dashiell. I'll send times this afternoon.
quality_notes: Urgency is real and specific (a stalled deal), the rep respects the CTO's authority rather than going around him, and the timeline offered is honest rather than inflated.

message: Hi Reuben, hope the caregiver scheduling rollout in Ohio is still going smoothly. You mentioned you're on the board of the state home care association. Any chance you'd be up for introducing us to one or two agency leaders there who are struggling with visit coverage? Totally fine if not.
quality_notes: Polite and references a real relationship channel, but asks for 'one or two leaders' without offering a reason they'd benefit or a way to make the intro effortless.

subject: Your 14 vendor MSAs are lonely
message:
Hi Matilda,

Confession: I peeked at your expired Draftkit trial. You uploaded 14 vendor MSAs in September, ran the clause comparison on exactly one, and then, I assume, got pulled into holiday-season contract chaos.

The one you ran flagged an uncapped indemnity and a 90-day auto-renewal notice window that's easy to miss. Statistically, a few of the other 13 probably have something similar.

I can reopen the trial for a week, or just run the comparison across all 14 and send you the flagged clauses as a PDF. Your call.

Leander
buyer_reply: Okay, that indemnity flag is exactly why I uploaded them. Send the PDF. If it's useful I'll get procurement involved.
quality_notes: Playful but grounded in the buyer's actual trial data, surfaces a concrete risk, and offers a no-effort deliverable that directly serves her work.

message: Imani, congrats on the new role at Shipyard. You'll obviously need Beacon CX like you did at your last company. Let's get the contract going so you're not flying blind. When can we start?
buyer_reply: Let's not get ahead of ourselves. I haven't even met the team yet.
quality_notes: Presumptuous: assumes the former champion will buy again and jumps to contracting before she's settled in or assessed her new team's needs.

message: Hi Bernard, Odalys Ferrer at Tallyhouse. Your former colleague Grace Mbatha at Harrowgate Trust suggested I call. She said Brightwater is getting a lot of grant-funded vendor spend and needs cleaner tracking for restricted funds. Grace's team uses us for exactly that. Call me at 503-555-0161 or reply to my email.
quality_notes: Clear and concise with a named referrer, but stops short of a specific outcome or a reason to call back now.

subject: An intro to Larkspur's operating team?
message:
Hi Annika,

Thanks for walking the Larkspur Equity team through your close process during their visit last week. Your controller told me the operating partner, Bernadette Cho, asked twice how you got from twelve days to five.

I know Larkspur has several other healthcare services companies in the portfolio, and from what Bernadette said, at least two are dealing with the same multi-location reconciliation problem you had before acquisitions were automated.

Would you be comfortable introducing me to Bernadette? I'd suggest a short note from you saying what's worked, and I'll take it from there. I won't ask her for a list of portfolio companies; I'd simply offer to share your playbook with any CFOs she thinks would benefit.

If you'd rather not mix your investor relationship with vendor conversations, I completely understand.

Cyrus
buyer_reply: Bernadette actually asked me for your contact already. I'll send the intro this afternoon and mention the acquisition piece specifically.
quality_notes: Spots a high-leverage referral path, uses an observed signal of interest, respects the sensitivity of the investor relationship, and makes the ask concrete.

message:
[Opening]
Hi Gustavo, it's Leontyne Bakker from Shiftwell. Do you have a few minutes, or would another time be better?

[If yes]
Thank you. I want to start by acknowledging how our last conversation ended. In February, you paused the Shiftwell evaluation because the nurses' union raised concerns that self-scheduling software would be used to cut hours or monitor staff. I appreciated that you put those concerns first, and I think it was the right thing to do at the time.

[Reason for call]
I'm calling because two things have changed, and I wanted you to hear them from me rather than in a generic email.

First, we've worked with two unionized hospital systems since then, and in both cases the union was part of the rollout. We built a configuration where seniority rules, overtime equalization, and minimum staffing ratios from the collective agreement are enforced by the system, so managers can't override them without a logged reason. Union reps actually got read access to the audit log.

Second, I understand your contract negotiations wrapped in September, so the timing may be different now.

[Question]
I'm curious, how is scheduling working for your units today? Are the issues we talked about earlier, the overtime costs and the last-minute agency fills, still there?

[Listen carefully. Take notes.]

[If yes]
That's what I suspected. Would it help if I connected you with the director of nursing operations at one of those systems? She can speak to how they handled the union conversation, which I think is the part that matters most for you. That would be a peer conversation, not a sales call, and I don't need to be on it.

[If no or uncertain]
That's helpful to know. Is there anything you'd want to see before you'd consider revisiting it?

[Close]
Thank you, Gustavo. I'll follow up with a short note summarizing what I mentioned about the union configuration, so you have it in writing.
quality_notes: Directly addresses the sensitive original objection, shows what has materially changed, and offers a peer reference on the exact concern rather than pushing a demo.

subject: Shelfwise App Marketplace + integrations
message:
Felicity,

Saw the announcement that Shelfwise is launching an app marketplace in Q2, with 30 partner integrations at launch.

When we spoke last fall, you had about a dozen integrations and decided to keep building them in-house. That made sense at that number. Thirty partners, each with their own auth, rate limits, and API versions, is a different maintenance load, and marketplace partners tend to expect faster turnaround than internal teams.

Patchbay's embedded integration product lets your team ship partner connectors on shared infrastructure, with monitoring and retries handled for you. A retail software company about your size went from roughly six weeks per integration to under two.

Worth 30 minutes before you finalize the marketplace architecture?

Jarrah
quality_notes: Specific trigger, recalls the prior decision without arguing with it, explains why scale changes the calculus, and times the ask to an architecture decision.

message: Hi Rosamund, thanks for the trial feedback, really useful. You mentioned your CFO, Leopold, is the one pushing for unit-cost metrics per customer. Would you be open to looping him into a short call so we can show him that view directly? Happy to keep it 20 minutes.
buyer_reply: Maybe. Let me see what he's prioritizing this month and get back to you.
quality_notes: Reasonable upward intro request tied to something the buyer said, but doesn't help the champion sell the meeting internally or explain what's in it for Leopold.

message: Elodie, Quorum HQ here again. Need an answer by EOD on whether you want a demo. Board season is coming!!
buyer_reply: STOP
quality_notes: Demands an answer by an arbitrary deadline over SMS with generic urgency and no context, prompting an opt-out.

message:
[Ximena on camera, with a laptop beside her]

Hi Thorsten, I'm Ximena from Fieldnote. Hannah Delacroix at Pebblebox mentioned you two were comparing notes on running research with parents and teachers, and she asked me to send you something short, so here it is.

Quick background on Hannah's team. They were running about ten parent interviews a month, and the insights lived in a mix of Notion pages and the notes app on whoever's phone. When they decided to redesign their onboarding, nobody could find what parents had said about the first week, so they ran the same interviews again.

[Turn laptop to camera]

This is what their workspace looks like now, using sample data. Every interview is transcribed and tagged, so when someone asks "what do teachers say about setup time," they get the clips and quotes across every interview, not just the most recent ones.

[Back to camera]

I don't know whether Sproutlearn has the same problem. Hannah mentioned you have one researcher and a lot of PMs who also do interviews, which is usually when it gets messy, because everyone has their own system.

If it's useful, I'd be happy to do a 20-minute call where you tell me how research works today, and I'll tell you honestly whether Fieldnote would help or whether it's too early for you. Hannah also said she's happy to jump on a call herself if you'd rather hear it from a peer.

Link to book time is below. Thanks, Thorsten.
quality_notes: Warm-intro video that tells the referrer's story concisely, shows rather than tells, connects to the buyer's team structure, and offers an honest fit check.

message: Kasimir, quick update: Ines at Harrow Health signed on today after your intro. Thanks for vouching. Owe you one, and I'll make sure their team takes good care of the auditor you recommended too.
quality_notes: Closes the loop on a successful referral promptly and specifically, building goodwill for future introductions.

message: Hector, I saw Signalcrest pre-announced Q3 below guidance and cited deal slippage. Not reaching out to pile on. When we spoke in spring you thought rep commits were good enough. If you're now rebuilding the forecast process, I'd be glad to share what slip-rate patterns usually show up in ad tech pipelines. Useful?
quality_notes: Sensitive handling of a public miss, connects it to the original objection without gloating, and offers relevant insight as the opening.

subject: New company, same onboarding headaches?
message:
Hi Pieter,

Saw you joined Coinwell as VP People. Congrats! Loved working with you at Marrowfield, and I still use your "day one should feel like day thirty" line in every discovery call.

No agenda here beyond saying hi. That said, if Coinwell's onboarding turns out to be the usual mix of spreadsheets and IT tickets, you know where to find me. Happy to grab a coffee and hear what you're walking into.

Calla
buyer_reply: Ha, you're quoting me to strangers now? Coinwell is exactly spreadsheets and IT tickets. Coffee next week, I'll buy.
quality_notes: Light, authentic re-engagement with a former champion that leans on shared history and leaves the pitch implied rather than forced.

subject: Following Up Regarding Your Tallyhouse Trial Experience and Next Steps
message:
Dear Ms. Okoro,

I hope this email finds you well and that you are having a productive quarter. I am writing to follow up regarding your recent trial of the Tallyhouse procurement and vendor spend management platform, which concluded several weeks ago.

As you may know, Tallyhouse is a comprehensive, best-in-class solution that enables organizations of all sizes to streamline procurement processes, gain visibility into vendor spend, enforce compliance with purchasing policies, manage contracts and renewals, automate approval workflows, and integrate seamlessly with existing ERP and accounting systems. Our customers consistently report significant time savings and cost reductions.

We understand that evaluating new software is a significant undertaking, and we want to ensure that you have all of the information necessary to make an informed decision. To that end, I have attached our product brochure, a pricing overview, a security whitepaper, and three customer case studies for your review.

I would be delighted to schedule a follow-up call at your earliest convenience to discuss your experience with the trial, answer any questions you may have, and explore how Tallyhouse can best support Calderwood Pharma's procurement objectives going forward.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Montgomery Ashby
quality_notes: Long, generic, and attachment-heavy; never mentions what the buyer did in the trial or why it stalled, and reads like a template sent to every expired trial.

message:
[Opening]
Hi Tamsin, this is Rafferty Olawale from Beacon CX. Gwendolyn Ashe at Northfield Partners connected us by email last week. Is now still a good time?

[If yes]
Great, thank you for making the time. Gwendolyn mentioned two things: that Callstream's board has been asking for a clearer view of net retention by segment, and that your team recently moved from a pooled CS model to named CSMs for your top 200 accounts. Is that right?

[Listen and confirm]

[Discovery]
I'd love to understand how that's going. With named CSMs, how are they deciding where to spend their time each week?

[Listen]

And when the board asks about retention, what are you able to show them today versus what you wish you could show them?

[Listen]

Last question: when an account churned in the last couple of quarters, how early did your team know it was at risk?

[Listen]

[Reflect back]
So if I'm hearing you right, the CSMs have relationships now, but they're relying on gut feel and whatever comes up in calls to prioritize, and you don't have a consistent signal to show the board ahead of time. Is that fair?

[Bridge]
That's the gap Beacon is designed for. We combine product usage from your platform, support data, and billing into a health score per account, and roll it up by segment. Two of Northfield's other portfolio companies use it for exactly the board view Gwendolyn mentioned.

[Ask]
I'd suggest a working session, about 45 minutes, where we look at a sample of your top 200 accounts and see how a health model would score them. You and one of your senior CSMs would be ideal. Would the week of the 8th work?

[Close]
Thanks, Tamsin. I'll send a recap and copy Gwendolyn so she knows we connected.
quality_notes: Uses investor-provided context to frame good discovery, reflects back what the buyer said before bridging, and proposes a practical working session with the right people.

message: Good morning, Mr. Asante. This is Philomena Garvey with Draftkit. I understand you joined Altimere as General Counsel this autumn; congratulations. Altimere's commercial team evaluated Draftkit last year for supplier agreements. I would welcome the chance to share what they found and hear your priorities. I can be reached at 206-555-0187. Thank you.
quality_notes: Courteous and appropriate for a GC, but vague about what the prior evaluation found, giving the buyer little reason to return the call.

message: Hi Jessica! Following up on our conversation about Ledgerline for Sunvale Energy. Still interested in automating your month-end close? Let me know when works for a call.
buyer_reply: My name is Ophelia and I work at Brightacre. I don't think we've ever spoken.
quality_notes: Copy-paste error with the wrong name and company, destroying credibility instantly and revealing the outreach as mass-produced.

message:
[Seraphina holds up a whiteboard that reads "Ashgrove: 22 integrations, 0 pager alerts in Nov"]

Hi Aldous! Seraphina from Patchbay. I'm told whiteboards are the official language of higher ed IT, so I came prepared.

So, first: that number is real. November was the first full month with zero sync failure alerts from the student information system integrations. When we started, you were averaging one a week, usually at 2 a.m. during registration. That's your team's work, and I'm genuinely happy for you.

[Flip whiteboard: "The ask"]

Here's my ask. You mentioned the regional university IT consortium meets in January, and that a few of the other schools are still running nightly batch scripts between their SIS and LMS. Would you be open to sharing what you did? Not a sales pitch. More like a ten-minute "here's what worked for us" segment. I'd be happy to build the slides for you, with your numbers, and you can cut anything that feels too vendor-y.

[Flip whiteboard: "No pressure"]

And if that's not your style, totally fine. Just tell me and I'll still bring donuts to your next team retro.

Thanks, Aldous!
quality_notes: Fun and visual without losing substance; celebrates a real customer metric, proposes a specific, low-effort way to share it at a relevant forum, and makes saying no easy.

message: Hi Noelani, Tavish from Pipewise. Heard you hired 6 AEs this quarter. Ready to revisit forecasting now that the team's bigger?
buyer_reply: Not really. Still happy with what we built in the CRM, and budget's spoken for until April.
quality_notes: Uses a relevant trigger but jumps straight to the ask without explaining why a bigger team changes the forecasting picture, inviting an easy no.

message: Marek, your Head of People, Esther, asked me to reach out. She's evaluating Onramp for onboarding checklists, but she was clear the decision depends on whether you're comfortable with how it provisions accounts and laptops. Could we do 20 minutes so you can poke holes in it before she goes further?
quality_notes: Internal referral that correctly identifies the IT director as a gatekeeper and invites scrutiny, which builds trust with a technical stakeholder.

subject: Introduction from Ms. Haverford
message:
Dear Mr. Drummond,

Theodora Haverford, who serves on both Corran's board and the board of Ellsworth Materials, suggested I write. She mentioned that Corran's audit committee materials are currently assembled from several sources and distributed by email, and that she has found the process at Ellsworth, which uses Quorum HQ, considerably easier as a director.

I would value the opportunity to understand how your team prepares board and committee materials today, and to share how Ellsworth structured its committee workspaces and access controls. Would a 30-minute conversation in early December be convenient?

With kind regards,
Augusta Penhaligon
buyer_reply: Ms. Penhaligon, Theodora raised this with me directly as well. Let's speak; please coordinate with my assistant, Mr. Lowell, for a time the week of December 7th.
quality_notes: Board-member referral is the strongest possible signal for this product; the message states it precisely and makes a modest, well-timed ask in an appropriate register.

subject: Fair workweek rules start Jan 1 in two of your markets
message:
Hi Dmitri,

Two of Brazen's markets have predictable scheduling ordinances taking effect January 1: schedules posted 14 days in advance, and premium pay when shifts change with less than that notice.

When we talked in the summer, your GMs were posting schedules about five days out. If that's still the case, those stores will owe premium pay on almost every change starting in six weeks.

Shiftwell tracks posting windows and calculates premium pay automatically, and flags changes that would trigger it before a manager publishes. Could we talk this week about what a rollout for just the affected stores would look like?

Kirsten
buyer_reply: We're aware of the ordinances. Legal is working on a policy. I'll forward to our ops lead in those markets, but no promises.
quality_notes: Urgency is legitimate and specific, but the email assumes nothing has changed since summer and doesn't acknowledge the buyer's likely existing plans, so it gets a polite forward rather than engagement.

subject: Regarding the stalled Clearstack evaluation
message:
Dear Ms. Lindholm,

I am writing regarding the Clearstack evaluation that your former FinOps lead, Arvid Sato, was running before his departure in August.

Frankly, the evaluation stalled because Arvid did not secure engineering buy-in or follow through on the data access we requested, and we were unable to complete the business case. Now that he has left, I believe the project deserves a fresh start with proper executive sponsorship.

Given Cargolink's cloud spend, which Arvid estimated at over $600K per month, I would like to schedule a meeting with you and your CTO to restart the process.

Sincerely,
Percival Oduya
buyer_reply: I'm not comfortable with a vendor criticizing a former employee or sharing internal figures he gave you. We'll pass.
quality_notes: Blames the departed champion, discloses internal numbers the buyer didn't share, and asks for a CTO meeting without establishing any value, alienating the new contact.

message: Hi Obinna, noticed Roamly just posted roles for two UX researchers. Congrats on growing the team! When we chatted last year you said research was mostly PMs doing ad hoc calls. Worth reconnecting once the new folks start?
quality_notes: Spots a good trigger and references the earlier conversation, but doesn't explain what changes for Roamly with a dedicated research team or offer anything concrete.

subject: Not a pitch
message:
Hi Thelonius,

I read your team's post-incident write-up from last week. It was clear, honest, and a lot more transparent than most companies manage. I'm sorry you've had to deal with it.

I'm not writing to sell you anything right now. You've got more urgent priorities, and the last thing you need is vendors circling.

When we talked in the spring, you mentioned that your access reviews and offboarding were still manual, and the write-up suggests the incident started with a stale contractor account. If, once things settle, you want help making access reviews continuous rather than quarterly, I'm here. Until then, if there's a template or checklist from our side that would be useful to you, just ask and I'll send it, no strings.

Agnieszka
quality_notes: Handles a sensitive trigger with genuine restraint, links it carefully to a prior discussion, and leads with no-strings help rather than a meeting request.

message: Rosalie, Fintan from Tallyhouse. You said to check back after your ERP migration. Is it done? Our ERP connector is now native, with no middleware, which was your main concern.
buyer_reply: Done as of last week. Send me times for a call in December.
quality_notes: Brief, honors the buyer's own requested timing, and addresses her specific prior objection in one line.

subject: Who else should be using this?
message:
Hi Bastien,

Your team's at-risk alerts helped save the Ridgeline Homes renewal last month. That one account was more than your annual Beacon contract.

Do you know any CS leaders at other construction or field services software companies who'd benefit from hearing that story? A name or two would be great, and I'm happy to send you a short blurb you can forward.

Thanks,
Lorelei
quality_notes: Strong, concrete proof point and helpful offer to draft a blurb, but the ask feels abrupt and slightly transactional right after the win.

message:
[Opening]
Good afternoon, Ms. Abernathy. This is Caspar Lindqvist from Draftkit. Ambrose Tiernan at Ridgeback Energy mentioned he had spoken with you about our work together and suggested I call. Is this a convenient time for a few minutes?

[If yes]
Thank you. I will be respectful of your time.

[Context]
Mr. Tiernan's legal department at Ridgeback adopted Draftkit about 18 months ago, primarily for vendor and interconnection agreements. Their main challenge was that the commercial team would send contracts to legal at the last minute, and the attorneys were spending most of their time on routine redlines rather than on the higher-risk terms.

They established a clause playbook with approved fallback positions, which allowed the contracts managers to resolve the routine items themselves and escalate only genuine deviations. Mr. Tiernan reports that attorney time on standard vendor agreements fell by roughly half.

[Discovery]
I do not want to assume your circumstances are the same. May I ask how Coastline's legal department handles incoming commercial agreements today?

[Listen]

How are fallback positions documented, if they are documented at all?

[Listen]

And where is the greatest strain on your team at the moment: volume, turnaround expectations, or consistency across attorneys?

[Listen]

[Bridge]
Thank you, that is very helpful. Based on what you have described, it may be worth looking specifically at how Ridgeback structured its playbook for the agreements that most resemble your highest-volume category.

[Ask]
Would you be open to a 45-minute session, perhaps with one of your senior contracts managers, where we walk through that approach? If it would be useful, Mr. Tiernan has offered to join for part of it.

[If she prefers to defer]
I understand completely. May I send a brief written summary of Ridgeback's approach for your review in the meantime?

[Close]
Thank you, Ms. Abernathy. I will confirm by email this afternoon.
quality_notes: Formal register suited to senior counsel, uses the referrer's results as context, asks focused discovery questions, and offers a peer-led session with a graceful fallback.

message: Knock knock! Who's there? Your expired Quorum HQ trial! 😂 Haha but seriously Fiorella, board decks are boring, and we make them less boring. Wanna chat? 🚀🚀
quality_notes: A forced joke and emoji spam to a CEO, with no reference to anything she did in the trial or a reason to re-engage.

message: Hey Sabine, Rocco from Onramp here! Hope you're crushing it. So I saw Halberd is opening a new office in Austin, which is super exciting, and I wanted to reach out because Onramp is the leading all-in-one employee onboarding and IT provisioning platform that helps fast-growing companies like yours automate account creation, device shipping, app access, checklists, and so much more, with over 200 integrations and an award-winning support team, and we've helped hundreds of companies cut onboarding time by up to 70 percent, so I'd love to set up a quick 30-minute demo to show you everything. Give me a call back at 737-555-0114, that's 737-555-0114. Talk soon!
quality_notes: Runs a decent trigger straight into a breathless feature list and unverifiable claims; nothing ties it to Halberd's actual onboarding situation.

message:
[Opening]
Hi Pilar, it's Evander Kristiansen from Ledgerline. We last spoke in January. Have you got a few minutes?

[If yes]
Thanks. When you decided to go with the close module that came with your ERP rather than Ledgerline, your reasoning was sound: one vendor, no extra integration, and it was included in your license. I'm not calling to second-guess that.

I'm calling because it's been about nine months, and I've found that's usually when teams know whether the bundled module is doing what they hoped. So I'm genuinely curious: how is it going?

[Listen]

[If "it's fine"]
Good to hear. Out of curiosity, where are you landing on days to close now, and which reconciliations are still mostly manual?

[Listen. If the answers suggest remaining pain, continue. If not, thank her and close.]

[If "it's been harder than expected"]
That's not unusual. What we tend to hear is that the module handles the checklist and the journal entries well, but the account reconciliations, especially inventory, freight accruals, and intercompany, still happen in spreadsheets because the matching logic isn't flexible enough.

Is that close to what you're seeing?

[Listen]

[Bridge]
Ledgerline can sit alongside the ERP module rather than replace it. Some customers keep the close checklist where it is and use us purely for the reconciliation matching. That's usually a smaller project than people expect.

[Ask]
Would it be worth 30 minutes to look at your three most painful reconciliations and see whether automating just those would make a real difference? If it wouldn't, I'll tell you.

[Close]
Thanks, Pilar. I'll send a short note with a couple of times.
quality_notes: Revisits a loss to a bundled alternative at a sensible interval, invites honest feedback, and offers a complementary, narrowly scoped option instead of a rip-and-replace.

subject: Intro to the claims team?
message:
Hey Olusegun,

Glad the payer connector rollout went smoothly last week, and thanks again for the candid feedback on the retry settings.

You mentioned the claims processing team is dealing with the same mess of one-off clearinghouse integrations your team had. Any chance you'd introduce me to their engineering lead? A quick Slack message would do it.

Delilah
buyer_reply: I'd rather not just yet. Their team is pretty protective and I want our rollout to bake for another quarter before I recommend anything internally.
quality_notes: Natural, brief internal referral ask built on a real comment, but slightly premature; it doesn't address the champion's political risk, which surfaces as the objection.

subject: Thank you, and one question
message:
Hi Gideon,

I wanted to say thank you for the intro to Paulina at Halverson Analytics. She and I met on Tuesday, and she's running a short pilot in January. Whatever happens, you made that easy.

Your note to her mentioned that your forecast accuracy improved to within 5 percent for three straight quarters. I hadn't heard you put it that way before, and it's a better summary than anything in our marketing.

One question, only if it's comfortable: would you be willing to let me use that line, attributed to you, in conversations with other CROs? If you'd prefer it stays anonymous, or not used at all, that's completely fine.

Thanks again,
Leocadia
quality_notes: Closes the loop on a referral with specifics, notices a powerful customer phrasing, and asks permission thoughtfully, offering anonymous or no-use options.

message: Hi Esperanza! Since you love Shiftwell, can you send me 5 names of other managers who need it? Thx!!
quality_notes: Presumes enthusiasm, demands an arbitrary number of names over SMS, and offers no context or reciprocity.

message:
[Ivo at his desk, screen-sharing a Clearstack dashboard with Genefold's trial data blurred for privacy]

Hi Larissa, Ivo from Clearstack. I'll keep this to about a minute.

Your trial ended three weeks ago, and nobody on your team has logged in since the first few days. That's fine. But before we delete the data, I wanted to show you the one thing it found.

[Zoom into a highlighted line]

This is a set of GPU instances tagged to your protein-folding pipeline. They've been running at under 5 percent utilization, around the clock, since at least August. At on-demand rates, that's a little over $19,000 a month.

It's possible there's a reason for it, like a reserved capacity commitment or a job queue I can't see. If so, ignore me. If not, that's worth a look regardless of whether you ever use Clearstack.

[Back to camera]

If you'd like, I can send the list of instance IDs so your team can check. And if you want to reopen the trial to see what else is in there, reply and I'll do it today.

Thanks, Larissa.
quality_notes: Revives a stale trial with one concrete, high-value finding, acknowledges what the data might not show, and leads with help the buyer can use immediately.

subject: The intercompany question you asked at booth 412
message:
Hi Dev,

Thanks for stopping by our booth at the Midwest Finance Leaders Summit on Tuesday. You asked a sharp question that I didn't answer well in the moment: whether Ledgerline can handle intercompany eliminations when two of your three entities run on different charts of accounts.

Short answer: yes, through a mapping layer that sits between the entity ledgers. The longer answer depends on how often your COA changes. If you're adding GL accounts monthly, the mapping needs an owner; if it's stable, it mostly runs itself.

I put together a two-page walkthrough of how a 240-person distributor with a similar setup cut their close from nine days to five. Happy to send it over, or walk through it live in 20 minutes if that's easier.

Either way, thanks for the good question.

Marisol
buyer_reply: Marisol, appreciate you circling back on that. Our COA changes maybe twice a year, so that sounds manageable. Send the walkthrough and I'll loop in our senior accountant, Renata. Could do next Thursday afternoon.
quality_notes: References a specific question from the booth conversation, gives an honest nuanced answer, and offers a low-friction next step. The buyer reply confirms relevance.

message:
[Open on Tanner sitting at a desk, a printed screenshot of the Lakeshore Inns careers page taped to the wall behind him]

Hey Gwen, Tanner here from Shiftwell. Quick video, under two minutes, I promise.

[Points to the printout]

So this is your careers page. I counted fourteen open front-desk and housekeeping roles across your properties on the north shore, and three of them were reposted in the last month. That usually tells me one of two things: either turnover is high, or the schedule is the thing people are leaving over. Often it's both.

Here's why I'm reaching out. We work with a few regional hotel groups, one of them about your size with eleven properties, and the pattern we saw was that managers were building weekly schedules in spreadsheets on Sunday nights, then spending Monday through Wednesday fielding swap requests by text. Staff felt like they had no say, and the managers were burned out.

[Leans in]

With Shiftwell, employees pick up and swap shifts from their phones, managers approve in one tap, and the system flags overtime before it happens instead of after payroll runs. That group cut their housekeeping turnover by about a fifth in the first two quarters. I won't pretend every property sees that, but it's a real number.

I'm not asking for a demo today. What I'd love is fifteen minutes to hear how scheduling actually works at Lakeshore right now. If it's already in great shape, I'll tell you we're not a fit and get out of your way.

There's a button right under this video to grab time, or just reply to the email. Thanks, Gwen.

[Waves, end]
quality_notes: Shows real research (careers page, reposted roles), ties it to a plausible pain, uses one credible proof point, and makes a modest ask. Natural, unscripted feel.

message:
[Elliot on camera, standing in front of a hotel lobby window, conference lanyard still around his neck]

Hi Camille, it's Elliot from Quorum HQ. We were on the same panel dinner last night at the Life Sciences Founders Forum, the one where the dessert took forty-five minutes. I'm recording this from the lobby before my flight because something you said stuck with me.

Pulling numbers from finance, chasing the clinical team for trial updates, reformatting slides, and then fielding three rounds of "can you also add" from your CEO. Department owners update their own sections in a shared template, you get a single board book with version history, and directors log in to one portal instead of digging through email.

[Pauses, softer]

Honestly, the bigger thing I heard was that you're tired. A pre-Series C biotech chief of staff is wearing about six hats. So I'm not going to push a demo. If it's useful, I'll send you the board book template we built with another clinical-stage company, no strings attached. You can steal the structure even if you never use us.

message:

subject: Your webinar question about contractor offboarding
message:

message:

message:
[Nolan seated in a conference room, neutral background, speaking directly to camera]

Good afternoon, Ms. Ramaswamy. My name is Nolan Whitaker and I'm with Draftkit. I'll keep this brief and respectful of your time.

I noticed from Bramblecrest's recent press release that you've taken on three new public infrastructure projects this year, including the transit station expansion. Projects of that kind typically bring a large volume of subcontractor agreements, each with indemnity, insurance, and change-order clauses that need review, and frequently on tight timelines driven by the general schedule rather than by legal.

Draftkit is a contract drafting and redlining tool built for in-house legal teams. Your team defines a clause playbook once, including your preferred positions and acceptable fallbacks, and Draftkit applies it when a subcontractor returns a redline. It highlights deviations, suggests your approved fallback language, and flags anything outside policy for attorney review. The goal is that your attorneys spend their time on the genuinely unusual terms, not on the fortieth version of the same insurance clause.

One general counsel at a regional contractor of similar size told us her team cut first-pass review time on subcontracts by roughly half, which mattered most during bid season.

I would welcome a twenty-minute conversation to understand how your team currently manages subcontractor paper, and whether this would be worth a closer look. If the timing is not right, I understand completely.

quality_notes: Formal tone fits a GC, the research is specific, the value is framed around attorney time, and the ask is modest. The buyer's timing objection is reasonable and clear.

message:

message:
[Rafael on camera, holding a printed copy of a conference agenda with one session circled]

Hi Ingrid, Rafael from Fieldnote. I was in the back row for your session at Roadmap Summit West, "We Interviewed 200 Teachers and Still Got It Wrong." Honestly one of the best talks of the conference.

[Sets the agenda down]

The part that stuck with me was your story about the gradebook redesign. Your researchers had actually heard the right insight in interviews eight months earlier, but it was buried in a doc nobody opened, so the team rebuilt the same assumption into the new version. You called it "institutional amnesia." I've been stealing that phrase all week, with credit.

That's the exact problem Fieldnote tries to solve. Interviews get transcribed and tagged into a shared repository, and when a PM starts scoping a feature, they can search across every past conversation. So "what have teachers said about grading on mobile" returns actual quotes and clips from the last two years, not just whatever the newest researcher remembers.

I don't want to oversell it. A repository only works if people actually tag consistently, and that's a process question as much as a tool question. Some teams nail it, some don't. I'm happy to share what the successful ones do differently, regardless of whether you use us.

If you're up for it, I'd love thirty minutes to hear how your research ops are set up today and maybe show you what your gradebook research would look like inside Fieldnote. Reply here and I'll work around your calendar.

Thanks again for the talk.
quality_notes: Attended the buyer's own session and quotes it accurately, maps her story directly to the product, and includes a credible caveat about adoption.

subject: Following our conversation at SecOps Northeast Summit
message:

message: Abdi, thanks for the conversation at the People Ops dinner in Brooklyn. message:
Opener:
"Hi Lillian, this is Cody Ferraro with Tallyhouse. We met at the Manufacturing CFO Roundtable in Cleveland last week. You were at my table during the working capital session. Do you have two minutes?"

If yes:
"Thanks. You mentioned that maverick spend on MRO supplies was something your audit committee flagged this year, with plant managers buying direct from local distributors on corporate cards. I wanted to follow up on that specifically."

Value:
"What we typically see at plants your size is that the spend itself isn't the problem, it's that it's invisible until the card statement comes in. Tallyhouse puts a lightweight request step in front of it. Plant managers still buy what they need, but the purchase routes to a preferred supplier or a catalog item when one exists, and anything over a threshold gets a quick approval. One plastics manufacturer in Indiana brought off-contract MRO spend from about thirty percent to under ten in two quarters."

Discovery questions:
"How many plants are we talking about? Is the card program centrally managed or per site? Who on your team owns the response to the audit committee?"

Ask:
"Would it be worth a thirty-minute session with you and whoever owns that audit response, to look at what it would take to get ahead of it before next year's review?"

If not now:
"Totally fair. When does the audit committee meet next? I'll send you the Indiana case study now and check in a few weeks before."

Voicemail fallback:
"Lillian, Cody from Tallyhouse, we met at the CFO Roundtable in Cleveland. Following up on the MRO card spend topic. I'll send a short case study by email. 555-0193."
quality_notes: Well-structured script anchored in a real event detail, with discovery questions, a specific proof point, and graceful branches for 'not now' and voicemail.

message:
[Trevor at his desk, the proposal PDF visible on a second monitor behind him]

Hi Natasha, it's Trevor. I just sent over the Beacon CX proposal and I wanted to walk you through the three things that actually matter in it, so you're not digging through twelve pages to find them.

One, pricing. We scoped it to your forty CSM seats plus read-only access for the account management team, since you mentioned they need to see health scores before renewal conversations. That read-only tier isn't something we normally include at no cost, but given the size of the book, we built it in.

Two, implementation. We're proposing six weeks, not four. I know your team wanted faster. The reason is your product usage data lives in a warehouse table that needs some cleanup, which your data team confirmed on our call Tuesday. Rushing that is how health scores end up wrong and CSMs stop trusting them. I'd rather take two extra weeks than lose your team's confidence in month two.

Three, success criteria. We wrote in the goal you gave us: flag at-risk accounts at least ninety days before renewal, with a target of catching eighty percent of logo churn in the at-risk segment. If we're not tracking toward that by day ninety, there's a review clause that lets you adjust or exit.

[Leans back]

What I'd love is twenty minutes with you and your ops lead, Hamid, to pressure-test the timeline before it goes to procurement. I'll send a couple of times. Thanks Natasha.
buyer_reply: Thanks Trevor. The six-week explanation makes sense. Hamid and I can do Monday at 11. One question I'll want to cover: is the review clause tied to a specific metric or is it subjective?

message:
